 Dated this the 9th day of June 2025
 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.130/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 18/06/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 29/12/2016 at about 12:30 p.m., while he was walking through the side of Kalady- Malayattoor road and when he reached the place by name Neeleswaram,
motorcycle bearing registration no.KL179448 ridden 2025:KER:40261 MACA NO. 548 OF 2020 by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
The incident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the second respondent.
A sum of 8,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/rider filed a joint written statement contending that the incident occurred due to the negligence of the claim petitioner.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
It was contended that the incident occurred due to the negligence of the claim petitioner.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A9 and Ext.C1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on a consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found 2025:KER:40261 MACA NO. 548 OF 2020 negligence on the part of the second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,71,295/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a coolie aged 56 years, was earning 30,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal, fixed the notional income at 9,000/-, which, even going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Allian. Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, 2025:KER:40261 MACA NO. 548 OF 2020 is quite low and hence requires to be enhanced.

sentences.text: In the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), I find that an amount of 10,500/- can be fixed as the notional income of the claim petitioner.
Loss of earnings It is pointed out that though an amount of 5,00,000/- was claimed under this head, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 45,000/- only.
This again is challenged.
Ext.A6 discharge summary reveals that the claim petitioner had sustained 'fracture both bone lower 1/3rd left leg'.

Ext.A6 further states that the claim petitioner was treated with wound debridement,
suturing of puncture wound, MIPPO plating left tibia and IM nailing left fibula of fracture both bone L/3 left lower leg and BK POP slab application.
The materials on record reveal that he had undergone two surgeries and was hospitalized for a period of 6 days.
Therefore, in all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 6 months.

Therefore, he can be granted 2025:KER:40261 MACA NO. 548 OF 2020 compensation towards loss of earnings for a period of 6 months which is 63,000/- (10,500 x 6).
Loss of amenities
Though an amount of 5,00,000/- was claimed under this head, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 65,000/- which is also stated to be on the lower side.
Taking into account the age, the injuries sustained and the medical interventions undergone by the claim petitioner, I find that an amount of 75,000/- would be just and reasonable.

10. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent:

 suffering (No  Modification)

(No  Modification)

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the 2025:KER:40261 MACA NO.
548 OF 2020 compensation by a further amount of 44,200/- (total compensation 4,15,495/- that is, 3,71,295/ granted by the Tribunal + 44,200/-
granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 50 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
